question: When was Masjid al-Aqsa built, if the hadith says it came 40 years after the Ka'bah?
answer:
When was it built? I said I'm not going to go into history, but we have to just mention a hadith about the history. We're not going to go into the detailed history, but when was it built? Well, the hadith mentions a very interesting fact that later commentators have discussed in a lot of detail.

The hadith is in Sahih Bukhari. Abu Dharr al-Ghifari asked the Prophet ﷺ, "O Messenger of Allah, which mosque was built first?", the first mosque built on earth. So our Prophet ﷺ responded, "Al-Masjid al-Haram," which is the Ka'bah. Then he said, "Which one was next?" So the Prophet ﷺ said, "Al-Masjid al-Aqsa." Here the term Masjid al-Aqsa is used. It is also the Qur'anic term: "Subhan alladhi asra bi-'abdihi laylan min al-Masjid al-Haram ila al-Masjid al-Aqsa." So this is a Qur'anic term as well. Abu Dharr al-Ghifari then said, "What was the time frame between building the Ka'bah and building Masjid al-Aqsa?" So our Prophet ﷺ said, "Forty years," arba'una sanah.

Now, this hadith, reported in Bukhari and Muslim, has caused a lot of commentators to go into various opinions. Because some people said: how do we understand this 40 years, when the Ka'bah was built by the Prophet Ibrahim 'alayhi al-salam, and the temple in Jerusalem was built by Solomon, Sulayman, and the time frame between Ibrahim and Sulayman is more than 1,000 years? Sulayman 'alayhi al-salam, one of the descendants of Prophet Ibrahim 'alayhi al-salam, is coming after him by many, many centuries; at least 1,000, if not 2,000 years between Ibrahim and Sulayman. So how do we understand the Prophet saying 40 years? This has led to a number of discussions.

One opinion is that we are talking about the original building of the Ka'bah. There is an apocryphal story (it's not authentic, it's not something that is ascertained, but it might be true) that Adam was the first to worship in this location. It's not that he built a structure, but that he was there and he sanctified the location. And so one theory goes, and this is what al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar and others also support, that the 40-year gap is between Adam 'alayhi al-salam in Makkah and maybe one of the sons of Adam (maybe Shith, they said, or others; Seth, they say in English, or Shith in Arabic), that he might have been in Masjid al-Aqsa. And it is not as if they built a structure, but rather that they prayed there and they sanctified it, and they were the first to bless that land. So this is one opinion.

Another opinion, and Ibn Taymiyyah seems to lean towards this: Ibn Taymiyyah says that Ibrahim 'alayhi al-salam built the Ka'bah with Isma'il 'alayhi al-salam, and then later on in his life, he also laid the foundations, or he prayed or he sanctified the area that is now Masjid al-Aqsa. And so it is Ibrahim 'alayhi al-salam.

And his student Ibn al-Qayyim championed yet a third theory, which is, I think, the one that makes quite a lot of sense to me, and Allah knows best. We do not know; we were not there. But Ibn al-Qayyim says no, it wasn't Ibrahim; it was rather his grandson Ya'qub, Ya'qub the son of Ishaq. And this actually makes a lot more sense: that the Prophet Ibrahim 'alayhi al-salam built the Ka'bah, and then Ya'qub. And we know for a fact that Ya'qub was the one living in that land. In fact, it is called after him, Bani Isra'il; that area, that region, is called after him. Ya'qub: Isra'il is his title. Ya'qub was living in that land and in that region.

And we can assume that he would have built at least, if not physically built, he would have had a piece of land in which they worshipped Allah, right? We would call it a masjid. They would call it something else back then, but it is the concept that there is a plot of land, there is a holy area where he and his descendants and the believers with him would worship Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. Not that he built a magnificent temple. Maybe there was nothing there. Maybe it was just an empty plot. Maybe it was just a few bricks. But the point is that something was there that identified that area, and that is now called Masjid al-Aqsa.

And to me, this opinion makes the most sense, and Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala knows best: **that the Prophet Ibrahim was the one who built the Ka'bah, an actual structure, and then his grandson Ya'qub, around 40 years later, built or consecrated that area that is called Masjid al-Aqsa.**
